nodes.name: NiS electrodeposition on NF
nodes.procedure: Clean NF pieces (99.99%, 80–110 ppi, 1.6 mm thick) with geometric area of 12 cm² placed in cathodic compartment of 3D-printed flow cell (inter-electrode gap 5 mm). Three pieces of Pt gauze (99.9%, 52 mesh) stacked in anodic compartment. FAA-3-50 AEM (50 μm) between compartments to avoid Pt incorporation. Plating bath (100 mL): 10 mM Ni(NO₃)₂, 0.5 M thiourea (CH₄N₂S), 100 mM phosphate buffer (pH 8.0) recirculated via peristaltic pump. Chronopotentiometry (CP) at -50 mA cm⁻², 25°C, three-electrode setup with Ag/AgCl reference. Optimized: 30 min deposition, 6 L h⁻¹ flow rate. Post-deposition: rinsed with DIW, stored in vacuum desiccator (25°C).

nodes.name: Sequential NiSP electrodeposition on NF
nodes.procedure: Two-step sequential electrodeposition on clean NF (12 cm²) in same 3D-printed flow cell setup (5 mm gap, Pt gauze anode, AEM separator). Step 1 (Ni+S): 100 mL bath with 10 mM Ni(NO₃)₂, 0.5 M thiourea, 100 mM phosphate buffer (pH 8.0). Step 2 (Ni+P): in situ bath change to 10 mM NiSO₄, 100 mM NaH₂PO₂·H₂O, 100 mM acetate buffer (pH 3.6). Both steps: CP at -50 mA cm⁻², 30 min each, 6 L h⁻¹ flow, 25°C, three-electrode with Ag/AgCl. Final rinse with DIW, vacuum desiccator storage (25°C).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiP/NF shows surface covered by grains 80-250 nm with abundant nanosheets in beehive-like pattern. NiS/NF shows comparable grains protruding from NF backbone without abundant nanosheets. NiSP/NF shows nanosheet arrays covering grains with increased roughness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the case of NiP (Fig. 2a), the surface was covered by numerous grains with sizes ranging from 80 to 250 nm. These particles are covered by abundant nanosheets following a beehive-like pattern... Finally, by carrying out an additional electrodeposition step of P to the NiS film, the morphology is modified further as depicted in Fig. 2c.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of S and P revealed in NiP/NF, NiS/NF, and NiSP/NF electrodes with small amount of oxygen indicating partial oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM-EDX elemental mappings clearly revealed a uniform distribution of S and P in the synthesized electrodes, as shown in Fig. 2e–g. Interestingly, mappings also revealed a small amount of oxygen in the materials, which suggests that partial oxidation occurred.

nodes.characterization_summary: Only three diffraction peaks at 44.2°, 52°, and 76.4° attributed to cubic Ni metal (ICDD PDF# 04-0850). No intense peaks for NixPy nor NixSy species found.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Only three diffraction peaks at 44.2, 52, and 76.4° can be seen, which are attributed to cubic Ni metal (ICDD PDF# 04-0850). No intense peaks neither for NixPy nor NixSy species were found.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiSP exhibits lattice fringes corresponding to (202) Ni12P5, (212) Ni2P, (210)/(200) Ni3S2, (312) NiSO4, and (113) Ni3(PO4)2. SAED pattern confirms polycrystalline nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images of NiSP exhibit lattice fringes corresponding to the (202) facet of Ni12P5, the (212) facet of Ni2P, the (210) and (200) facets of Ni3S2, the (312) facet of NiSO4 and the (113) facet of Ni3(PO4)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDX mappings demonstrate presence of Ni, S, P, and O atoms in NiSP/NF material.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM-EDX elemental mappings demonstrate the presence of Ni, S, P, and O atoms in the material (Fig. 2j).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p3/2 peaks: ~852.4-852.8 eV (Ni–S/Ni–P), ~855.3 eV (Ni(OH)2), ~856.6 eV (Ni3(PO4)2), ~857.0 eV (NiSO4). P 2p shows nickel phosphide and phosphate doublets. S 2p shows nickel sulfide, S–O, and nickel sulfate. NiSP/NF Ni–S peaks shift to higher binding energies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p3/2 spectra displayed five peaks located at ∼852.4-852.8 eV for nickel sulfide (Ni–S) or nickel phosphide (Ni–P), ∼855.3 eV for Ni(OH)2, ∼856.6 eV for Ni3(PO4)2, ∼857.0 eV for NiSO4... Ni–S 2p3/2 and 2p1/2 peaks of the NiSP film slightly shifted toward higher binding energies compared to the NiS film.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiP film exhibits more amorphous nature with limited crystalline Ni12P5 spots. NiS film shows characteristic planes of Ni3S2 and NiSO4. NiSP film shows higher density of S/P-rich spots.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additional TEM images exhibited the characteristic planes of Ni3S2 and NiSO4 for the NiS film and Ni12P5 for the NiP film (Fig. S7†). Notably, the NiP film exhibited a more amorphous nature among the as-prepared films... Evidently, the NiSP film exhibited a higher density of S/P-rich spots.
